problem: Existing VLN methods do not explicitly mine the connection between rich historical observations and the current environment, and do not adaptively learn clues from history that are relevant to the current scene.
motivation: VLN is a sequential task where history holds contextual knowledge important for decisions. Using all history indiscriminately is noisy and costly, so the agent needs to decide when to use history and to distill it into a form the decision network can easily use.
key_idea: Use action-distribution entropy to decide when to consult history, then convert historical context into prompt vectors by sampling from an end-to-end learned, cross-task shared token library.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that discretizing history into learned prompt tokens gives a compact, knowledge-rich representation the decision network can use more easily. It also claims that sharing the token library across tasks captures common features and improves generalization to unseen environments.
method: Entropy-based history acquisition: computes the uncertainty (entropy) of the previous step's action probability distribution to decide whether historical information is used at the current step.
Prompt generation module: transforms historical context into prompt vectors by sampling from a learned token library.
Learned token library: discrete tokens trained end-to-end, encoding semantic cues from historical observations compactly.
Cross-task shared token library: one library shared across R2R, REVERIE, SOON and R2R-CE to mine common features and improve generalization.
